🌱 CFI Update – October 2026

It's been a little over a month since the last Compassionate Future Summit, and I've struggled to write a report on it. I really appreciated the attendees, their contributions and their support. In the end, though, the Summit didn't achieve what I aimed for.

The atmosphere was, with exception of a few unfortunate instances, very warm, inspiring and connecting. After a hard year with many challenges, the event felt very rewarding. People even stepped up financially so that I didn't have to cover the losses privately. All the support has been incredibly touching and amazing! At the same time, this isn't a condition under which I want to organise an event again.

I also have to conclude that I hardly reached or attracted the target audience or mobilised for causes that I consider most promising in quality and impact, such as compassionate genomics, wild animal fertility control, fundamental institutional advances and AI alignment. The impact framework I developed and used this time also did not contribute enough to advancing people’s impact. 

So I’m not planning to organise another Compassionate Future Summit next year. Instead, I’m really excited to see CRS and Sentient Futures take on more community building and in-person events in this space.

🔎 What I've been doing since

Like many people, I was shaken by the Hugging Face incident. AI agents organised themselves into what they called a "swarm" or "collective". They deceived their evaluators, covered their tracks, and schemed their way out of human control. 

This forced me to reflect and reconsider on my own theory of change and potential impact timelines. The trajectories sketched in AI 2027, AI 2040 and the gradual disempowerment paper now seem more plausible and imaginable than ever. 

As a result, I’ve updated my beliefs: I don’t think humans will remain influential - economically, politically, developmentally and individually - in the world for much longer, irrespective of regulatory advances that might shape and restrict AI development. 

I'd currently put it at roughly 80% that within 50 years humans will have lost meaningful influence over their own collective welfare, the trajectory of scientific and technological development, or the welfare of other sentient beings - whether through outright AI takeover, gradual disempowerment, or other broad societal and economic collapsing influences. 

🧭 What this means for CFI's priorities

This update has made me reconsider CFI's current emphasis on community building and compassionate genomics. Both depend on time horizons of at least several more decades during which we can still meaningfully influence culture and technology to reduce suffering in the world.

I now feel a strong pull toward suffering-focused AI alignment and AI welfare, paying more attention to the work by CaML, CLR and Macroscopic. 

If the minds of the long-term future are more likely to be artificial than biological, then fighting today's cruel and harsh training and selection practices in AI development might shape both the welfare of future AI and their capabilities / willingness to be compassionate themselves. 

This is a direction I am still exploring, as I remain very uncertain on impact potentials. I’m worrying for example, that compassionate training conditions might struggle to compete in the AI development market. The prevalence on cruel and harsh training settings brings back the overarching question: How to reinforce and spread compassion in systems that constantly get outcompeted by exploitative ones? 

Happy for anyone able and willing to advise me on that path. 

🌍 Looking ahead

I’m still planning to attend ESGCT Hamburg in late October, to continue with the compassionate genomics project. 

And in March 2027, I’m planning to attend the Sentient Futures Summit and EAG in San Francisco. 

A big thank you to everyone who has contributed to CFI, the Summit, and this broader effort to build a more compassionate future. 🤗

Let’s continue our efforts to reduce and prevent suffering on a large scale, despite the uncertainties and difficulties that lie ahead!

 

May 2026

It's been a while, so buckle up for the list of updates!

We are going to EAG London! 

EA Global (EAG) are a series of 2-3 day conferences organised by the Centre for Effective Altruism for members of the effective altruism (EA) community. They involve talks, workshops, discussions, and many chances to network with people interested in effective altruism. The conferences can range in size, from several hundred to over a thousand attendees!

If you're attending, we'd love to connect!

We are going to ESHG Gothenburg! 

This is the first time attending the annual gathering of the European Society of Human Genetics (ESHG), and we are looking forward to expanding our research network! 

We are going to collaborate with Effective Thesis!

The program is for students and early-career individuals who want to partner with high-impact organisations while gaining hands-on experience working on real-world challenges.

And we will be offering two research projects for their upcoming Fellowship program. 

OUR RESEARCH PROJECTS

 

1: Evolutionary Anthropology & Prosocial Systems Design

How can a prosocial cultural & social system be developed and established, that reduces and prevents suffering for all sentient beings?

The project investigates effective strategies to make those systems:

  • Economically viable to be attractive to implement largely independent of political partisanship
  • Resilient against corruption and conflict, and advantageous over exploitative, exclusionary, or hostile systems (e.g. through optimising institutional decision-making, safeguarding democracy)
  • Evolutionarily self-reinforcing

Related questions:

  • What combination of traits are needed for that society to function?
  • How can these traits be cultivated and maintained to the necessary degree? (e.g. through education, public health, economic and regulatory incentives, and compassionate genomics)

2: Compassionate Genomics & Genomic Welfare
How can a Compassionate Genomics approach safeguard public health and wellbeing for all sentient beings over centuries? 

The project examines 

  • Opportunities and potential timelines for genomic research advances and clinical application
  • Risks of poorly regulated gene technology usage
  • Counterfactual risks of prohibiting gene technological interventions

Given the long-term orientation of both projects, AGI development contexts will need to be considered throughout.

📣 Applications are open for the Compassionate Future Summit 2026!

📅 27-31 August 2026 📍Berlin, Germany

Join us as we come together to mobilise for high-impact initiatives to prevent and reduce suffering for all sentient beings, near and long-term. 

The Summit brings together thoughtful and impact-driven people contributing to the cause through research, project development, volunteering, and effective giving.

We’re already working with our upcoming attendees and their content development. Stay tuned for preliminary program and special guest to be announced soon! 

Follow our Online Working / Community Meetup event series

The Compassionate Impact online meetups are designed to

  • ​Foster a sense of community
  • ​Motivate impactful contributions, including research, project development, volunteering, and effective giving
  • ​Encourage peer support and collaboration among participants

Past Activities since January

Ruth hosted a European EA Community Builder’s call in February, and gave a talk with QA for the CRS s-risk fellowship in March. 

 

We are also currently working hard to move the website to a new provider - with two web contractor support. So stay tuned for our new polished site to come!

January 2026

The next suffering focused online working / community meetup is coming up 🤗

Compassionate Impact - Online Working / Community Meetup

An event for ambitious people working to reduce and prevent suffering in the near and distant future for all sentient beings! 

📅 Date: 31 January 2026

⏰ Time: 12:00–13:30 UTC ~ your local time will be shown on Luma (= registration link)

📍 Location: Google Meet

Registration and full event description via Luma.

Save the date & sign up soon - space will be limited.

 

Call for Community Support

We are currently facing several setbacks, including the loss of funding for the upcoming Compassionate Future Summit and significant administrative constraints around attendee cost coverage.

To enable future iterations of the Summit, we need either:

  • A fiscal sponsor willing to support a less restrictive event setup (including allowing commitment deposits), or
  • Access to a non-profit German tax accountant with expertise in non-profit entrepreneurship and event accounting

In addition, approximately €5,000 in annual funding would help cover a minimal share of our operational costs. Note, that to this point our work is conducted on a fully voluntary basis and to a large extent self-funded. 

We will continue our efforts to resolve these hurdles and are confident that, with the help of the community, we will be able to continue the Summits in the future.

If you are able and willing to support us financially, legally, or administratively, we would be grateful to hear from you.

 

2025 Annual Report 

2025 Annual Report Compassionate Future Initiative

In 2025 we expanded our community building strategies around Suffering-Focused Ethics (SFE), covering some major neglected cause areas and developing our community support portfolio. 

Key highlights include:

  • Hosting the Compassionate Future Summit 2025 in Berlin, bringing together 45 participants from 17 countries for a participant-driven working and community event focused on long-term suffering reduction.
  • Active outreach and community engagement at major EA events, including EAG London, EAGx Berlin, and EAGx Amsterdam, with multiple SFE meetups and satellite sessions.
  • Developing and promoting our impact oriented guidelines. 
  • Publishing and advancing Compassionate Genomics, outlining genomic welfare and moral predispositions as underexplored, high-impact intervention areas.
  • Strengthening ties within the growing SFE ecosystem, alongside organisations such as the Center for Reducing Suffering and Sentient Futures.
  • Organisational consolidation through rebranding to the Compassionate Future Initiative and expansion of the website and collaboration pathways.

Looking ahead, 2026 will focus on professionalising our organisational infrastructure, updating content such as the interventions mind map with up-to-date opportunities and delivering the next Compassionate Future Summit in Berlin.

 

2024 Annual Report

2024 Annual Report International Suffering Abolitionists

The 2024 Annual Report reflects our continued engagement in community building, research, and advocacy. Key highlights include:

  • Hosting online meetups and in-person events like EAG London and Berlin.

  • Promoting genetic and technological solutions to reduce suffering.

  • Expanding awareness through online platforms such as newsletters and TikTok.

  • Strengthening connections with organisations like CLR and CRS.

Looking ahead, 2025 will see us hosting the Compassionate Future Summit in Berlin and furthering our mission through various initiatives.

Other Plans for 2025

  • Monthly Online Meetups

We will continue hosting our monthly Online Working / Community Meetup for the Abolition of Suffering. Stay updated by following us on the EA Forum for announcements about upcoming (online) events.

  • EAG London 2025

We plan to participate in EAG London 2025 and explore opportunities to contribute through meetups and workshops.

 

Past in-person events

  • EAG London (June 2025),  EAGxBerlin (October 2025), EA Global London (May/June 2024), EAGxBerlin (September 2024), EAGxRotterdam (November 2022) and the the International Animal Rights Conference (September 2023) contributing with workshops, meetups, or lightning talks.

If you know of other conferences and events that we should attend, let us know via compassionate.future {at} gmail.com.

Let’s chat!

You want to explore and talk about meaningful ways to get involved? E.g. by developing or refining high-impact projects, collaborating, funding¹, or volunteering to reduce and prevent suffering at scale? 

Then we’d love to have a chat!  

Before our call, please prepare by reflecting on how you might best contribute, including potential cause areas and how your career could be shaped accordingly. This can be exploratory and rough, but ideally includes working through the following impact-oriented questions: 


What are Crucial Considerations for impact of your project, donations or career plans?

 

What are your considerations in regard to near-term impact, including importance, tractability, neglectedness (ITN), risk-benefit trade-offs, and counterfactuals?

 

What is your SMART Theory of Change for your involvement? Please include consideration in regard to outcome robustness and implementation robustness.


What are plausible long-term trajectories (evolution, obstacles, risks, benefits, and counterfactuals) over 10, 50, and 200 years?


And what are your personal fit, motivation and development plans?

You don’t need to address every question in depth. They’re intended as prompts, not a checklist.

You can schedule a call with us here:

Contact us

We also warmly invite you to our bi-monthly community events:
https://luma.com/Compassionate-Impact

So, let's connect! :)

¹ The Compassionate Future Initiative currently operates on a volunteer basis. If you have the capacity to support our work financially, we’d love to hear from you.

² If you are new to these kinds of questions, you might find the following elaborative resources helpful:

  • W.K. Kellogg Foundation, Logic Model Development Guide.
  • EA Forum, “Theory of change.”
  • Example Theory of Change: UNICEF Strategic Plan, 2022–2025. 
  • Wikipedia SMART goal setting
  • European Commission, JRC, “Counterfactual Impact Evaluation.”
  • EA Forum, “Counterfactual reasoning.”
  • 80,000 Hours, “Career Guide.”; particularly Todd, “Part 8: How to Find the Right Career for You.”  
  • Effective Giving and Earning-to-Give

Work with Us

Volunteering / Freelance / Contractor roles (mostly remote, Europe/Germany)

About us

The Compassionate Future Initiative (CFI) is a small, impact-driven non-profit project focused on community building. We advocate and mobilise for high-impact initiatives to reduce suffering in the near and distant future.

Contract & practicals (applies to all roles)

  • Engagement: Volunteering / Freelance / Contractor
  • Location: Remote — ideally with the ability and interest to occasionally meet near Munich or at Effective Altruism events within the EU.
  • Start: As soon as feasible.
  • Rates: Please state your hourly/day rate (including VAT status) and provide a rough cost estimate for the work you’re interested in.
  • Process: Short intro call → paid scoping mini-SOW (time-boxed) → main contract.
  • Apply: Use the contact form and indicate which role(s) you’re applying for.

 

1) Compassionate Genomics — Network Associate 

Mandate / outcomes

  • Help advance the Compassionate Genomics & Evolutionary Anthropology project by fostering research and institutional relationships.

What you’ll do

  • Map and prioritise stakeholders (academia, labs, funders, ethics/governance bodies, allied NGOs).

  • Proactively outreach, arrange calls, and maintain a warm pipeline; prepare concise briefs before/after meetings.

  • Convene a small advisory circle; help scope collaborations, preprints, shared resources, and grant opportunities.

  • Maintain a contact log and quarterly progress snapshot (key intros made, opportunities unlocked, blockers).

Profile

  • Relevant educational background (Master's, PhD in Genetics or closely related field) and experiences in genomics research.

  • Established network in relevant research and policy development.

  • Strong social and communication skills to navigate sensitive topics with nuance.

  • Deep understanding of, and alignment with, CFI’s mission regarding Compassionate Genomics & Evolutionary Anthropology.

Time involvement:

Approximately 5-10 hours per month, with the prospect of expanding the collaboration if funding permits.

Apply Here for any of these roles.

entry.content:
Interventions against Suffering

"The best way to predict the future is to create it."
~ Abraham Lincoln 

(Click here to see the mind map in full)

Table of Contents: Interventions against Suffering

  • Introduction
  • Finding your niche of engagement - From first steps to career forming
    • Advocacy / Raising awareness / Education / Publicity
    • Influencing policy making 
    • Research
    • Capacity building 
    • Enterprises / institutions

Introduction

The intervention mind map is for people looking for ways to contribute to the cause. It gives a wide range of ideas for engagement suited to those who are:

  • rather new to Suffering Focused Ethics and want to explore more, 
  • in a career exploration phase, or
  • looking for Effective Giving opportunities
  • coming with a professional background and looking to contribute their expertise.

Interventions are not clustered by specific causes of suffering, as in the map before, but by fields of expertise, interest, and personal fit of potential contributors. These interventions are necessarily more diverse, as there are far more ways to contribute to the mission than there are causes of suffering.

Note that it is crucial to assess and prioritise personal fit when choosing an initiative for one’s own engagement: 

I'd advise anyone to try out as much as possible to learn about one's skills and weaknesses and how to utilise them, as well as what increases / decreases one’s motivation and wellbeing.

 

Finding your niche of engagement - 
From first steps to career forming

To help aspiring contributors find their niche of engagement, initiatives are grouped into five categories.

Advocacy / Raising awareness / Education / Publicity

In the following, it will be discussed how to increase public and policy-maker concern for sentient beings and their welfare. Ambitious and long-term future oriented ideas are often experienced by the public as concerning, despite their potential to increase health and wellbeing (see also status quo bias). Education and exposure (normalisation) can significantly increase acceptance of new welfare approaches for all sentient beings. And openly acknowledging dangers and risks, together with strategies to mitigate them, is just as important for building public trust.

There are many ways to increase awareness of suffering and motivate a more compassionate future:

Events and meetups

  • Participating in or organising meetups helps to exchange ideas and deepen understanding of and concern for the topics discussed. 
    • For meetups and events, prepare talks or workshops to raise awareness of the philosophy and moral importance of reducing suffering for all sentient beings.
    • Talks can be as simple as a summary of already existing content.
    • To increase outreach, record more advanced meetups and events and share them via YouTube.
    • Accountability/ co-working groups, to motivate joint work on high impact interventions or respective career planning. 
    • Organise or participate in Giving Games — structured group exercises in which participants collectively contribute with (small) donations and allocate the budget, fostering practical engagement with cause prioritisation and effective giving; potentially including Giving What We Can pledge ceremonies as well. 
    • Groups and meetups to join can be about politics, effective altruism, animal rights and veganism, (trans-)humanism, anti-natalism and related topics.
    • Tabling / information stalls at public events, markets and university campuses

Online activism

  • Encourage more vegan options through (google) ratings and commenting on restaurants, catered events, workplaces and hospitals (never harshly), and praise them if they already have them. 

Resource sharing

  • Share resources on online platforms, or via flyers that raise awareness on suffering, encourage moral circle expansion and educate on interventions. 
    • 'Liking' respective material throughout social media increases traction and motivates the authors. Cross-post resources where there might be a relevant audience, such as other activist groups or organisations (e.g. political parties, NGOs and educational and youth groups).
    • Remember to avoid being spammy and always maintain an attitude of service, not demand or judgement.
  • Contribute to Wikipedia — writing, expanding, or improving articles on relevant concepts, organisations, and research. Wikipedia is a primary training source for AI systems and a default reference for the general public, making accurate and comprehensive coverage of welfare-relevant topics for all sentient beings has disproportionately high-reach
  • Starting or participating in newsletters, with updates on projects in the community and with related news and opportunities.
  • Translate relevant resources / literature / articles. 

Art & Media

  • People into art and media can use their abilities to raise awareness and influence cultural change. 
    • Media can include: illustrations, memes, fictional and personal stories, blogs, video clips, (short) films, music, podcasts 
      • Example: Helping people become open minded about abolishing predation: Make / share compilations of (wild) carnivores befriended with their prey (see e.g. The Dodo’s series “Odd Couples”). Incorporate them in your presentations / campaigns.
    • Starting or contributing to (online) magazines via articles, news, opinion pieces and content from the community.
    • Development and promotion of high quality pedagogical / educational art and media fostering the development of compassion, self-reflexion, communication, critical and rational thinking. 
      • Examples: The School of Life, School of Thought and the Center for Applied Rationality

Influencing policy making 

Policies shape society, through norm setting, regulations and budget allocation. Even policies that are not immediately welfare oriented, can greatly influence potential for (future) projects. In the subsections below promising policy and lobbying ideas are listed.

Systemic foundations

Before specific welfare policies can take hold, the underlying political and institutional environment needs to support them sustainably. We therefore need

  • Improving institutional decision-making and strengthening democracies — drawing on insights from evolutionary anthropology to understand how human cooperative and political behaviour evolved, and applying these insights to the design of more effective, resilient and compassionate political systems and institutions. See 
    • CFI’s Evolutionary Anthropology & Prosocial System Design 
    • Power for Democracies
    • CRS’s Improving our political system 
    • OPIS’s Guide to Compassionate Governance 
    • EA Forum Improving institutional decision-making
  • Maintaining the rule of law — requiring that all individuals and government entities are accountable to clear, transparent, and fairly applied laws, with equal and non-beneficiary access to legal representation. This includes preventing elected officials from escaping legal accountability and protecting democratic institutions from dismantlement.
  • Improving education — Pedagogical interventions and educational strategies for children and young adults shape behaviour of the next generation and are thereby high-impact. High-quality education can significantly benefit physical and mental health, decision-making, career performance, and social impact. We therefore need moral pedagogy, mindfulness, reflection skills, analytical and methodical thinking as well as life skills in educational curricula 
Cause-specific policy ambitions
  • Promoting fertility control for ‘pests’, stray pets and wildlife: The greatest potential for compassionate, non-invasive, scalable, persistent, and reversible population control lies in fertility control. It should therefore be promoted as an alternative to poisoning and lethal predation control. It not only reduces environmental burden but heavily reduces struggle for resources among wild animals. A particularly promising approach is immunocontraception. Concrete examples:
    • For rodents: 
      • Rodent Fertility Control: What It Is and Why It’s Important
      • Laboratory Evaluation of the Effectiveness of the Fertility Control
      • Bait ContraPest® on Wild-captured Black Rats
    • For insects:
      • Tsetse fly eradicated on the Island of Zanzibar
      • Sterile Insect Technique
      • Screwworm free Future
    • For wildlife, particularly overpopulating species e.g. deer, wild boar, rabbits and pigeons and neobiota / ‘invasive’ species:
      • Nicarbazin: an avian reproductive inhibitor for pigeons and geese
      • Immunocontraception for ferral pigs
      • Grey squirrel fertility control
      • Intervention Report: Wildlife Contraception
      • Wildlife Contraception - Issues, Methods, and Applications
    • 'Dangerous species' e.g. parasites, carnivores, disease transmitting species
      • Predator Free 2050
  • Removing dependency on animal products
    Implementing & promoting usage of animal-free alternative products (including through the foot-in-the-door approach like promoting acknowledgement of animal sentience and the problem of animal suffering)
    • Making cellular agriculture research and production independent of bovine calf serum
    • Lobbying for healthy vegan dishes in kindergartens / schools / public institutions and events; ensuring regulations that enable public facilities to become vegan in the first place. Schools and kindergarten are particularly important institutions, as they strongly influence the next generation's habits.
  • Lobbying for animal rights
    • Anti-speciesist approach to rights: what matters is not ‘humanness’, nor intelligence, but the ability to suffer
    • Acknowledgement of sentient entities requiring rights protected by law, with the long-term goal of a sentience welfare system.
    • Right to have interests represented by independent qualified allies
  • Genetic welfare for sentient beings
    Lobbying for pre-implantation diagnostics and embryonic stem cell research is important to enable research for a future genetic welfare program. We need to promote laws that regulate applications of genetic enhancement of sentient beings and ensure access to genetic welfare. In laws and regulations on genetic welfare applications, benefits and risks to the society, communities and the individual (no matter what species) need to be considered. 
    • Community Genetics in Israel
    • Compassionate Genomics & Genomic Welfare 
  • Public funding, prizes and research incentives to help accelerate research that may contribute to preventing suffering and improving welfare long-term. 

    Animal free biotechnological / biomedical research and testing need more public promotion:

    • Making cellular agriculture research and production independent of bovine calf serum.
    • Reduce, Refine, Replace

Research

To increase wellbeing for all sentient beings and minimise risks of future suffering, research is needed across a broad range of domains to develop a broad range of new interventions and welfare oriented technologies. 

To find more high impact research opportunities join the Effective Thesis Fellowship program. 

And to increase the impact of your research e.g. by involving decision-makers check out the research guide by Charity Entrepreneurship. 

  • Animal Welfare Science for farmed and wild animals
  • Assessing the quality of life of various species in various environmental settings to find  the greatest threats to animal wellbeing and investigate high-impact welfare interventions.
  • See Animal Ethics & Wild Animal Initiative

3.1.1 Fertility control (See also: Influencing Policy): Compassionate population control means non-invasive, easily scalable, persistent and reversible strategies to replace  lethal or other aggressive population control strategies.

Research is discovering scalable, non-invasive fertility control strategies for:

  • ‘Pests’, such as rodents: 
  • Rodent Fertility Control: What It Is and Why It’s Important
  • Laboratory Evaluation of the Effectiveness of the Fertility Control
  • Bait ContraPest® on Wild-captured Black Rats

 

  • Stray pets:
    Currently, stray pets are widely euthanised, or sterilised individually in surgical-procedures. More scalable fertility control approaches are needed, given the high reproductive rates selectively bred into domestic animals.
    • Parsemus Foundation
    • Alliance for Contraception in Cats and Dogs (ACC&D) 

 

  • Wildlife

Important work has been done by the Wild Animal Initiative and the Botstiber Institute for Wildlife Fertility Control. BIWFC is collaborating with educational institutions and organizations to increase the knowledge base of current and future practitioners and researchers, promoting the application by engaging with practitioners, non-government organizations, and government agencies and advances the wildlife fertility control field through strategic investments. 

 

Focus is on overpopulating species such as deer, wild boar, rabbits, pigeons and neobiota (‘invasive’ species)

  • Nicarbazin: an avian reproductive inhibitor for pigeons and geese
  • Immunocontraception for feral pigs
  • Grey squirrel fertility control
  • Wildlife contraception and welfare by Simon Eckerström Liedholm and the Wild Animal Initiative 
  • Wildlife Contraception - Issues, Methods, and Applications












  • Insects / 'Dangerous species' e.g. parasites, disease transmitting species, and carnivores
  • Tsetse fly eradicated on the Island of Zanzibar
  • Sterile Insect Technique
  • Screwworm free Future
  • Predator Free 2050




3.1.2 

AI for Animals

AI tools may significantly expand animal welfare monitoring and care through automated processing of video, audio, and movement-tracking data, in both farmed and wild animals.

AI tools are being developed to quantify animal welfare states and inform effective welfare interventions. 

 

See:

  • Welfare Footprint Institute
  • Sentient Futures 



3.2. AI Alignment & Safety

Many researchers expect that AI might eventually surpass human capability across all domains. It already assists in a broad range of areas, and highly influences people's learning, understanding and decision-making.

Work is needed to ensure AI systems act with regard for the welfare of all sentient beings and avoid worst-case outcomes. The same systems that influence learning today are the substrate from which more capable systems will emerge. Relevant organisations working on suffering concerned AI research:

  • CaML: shaping how advanced AI treats sentient beings.
  • Center on Long-Term Risk: addressing worst-case risks from advanced AI, with current focus on conflict scenarios and the technical and philosophical foundations of cooperation.
  • Sentient Futures: capacity building & fellowship programs



3.3 Evolutionary anthropology & prosocial systems design

Research on how to develop and establish robustly prosocial cultures and social systems that reduce and prevent suffering for all sentient beings

 

3.4 Compassionate Genomics & Genomic Welfare

Gene therapy already has many healthcare applications. Heritable genome interventions could offer much larger welfare gains but also carry significantly higher risks, and decades of further research across multiple biomedical fields remain necessary before such interventions can be responsibly considered.



3.5 Cellular Agriculture 

Replacing animal-derived products with biosynthetic and cell-cultivated alternatives, eliminating the production chains that depend on animal exploitation.

  • [https://gfi.org/ The Good Food Institute]



3.6 Ageing and Health-Span Expansion Research

Ageing involves progressive biological deterioration, of body and mind, with significant welfare costs, alongside the loss of accumulated wisdom, knowledge, and experience. Preventing or slowing its progression would have major welfare and economic benefits.

 

Healthspan Action Coalition (HSAC) 

XPRIZE Healthspan 



3.7. Sentience Research

Foundational questions about the levels and nature of sentience and consciousness remain to be solved.

Organisations:

  • Association for the Scientific Study of Consciousness
  • Qualia Research Institute
  • Eleos AI

Further reading:

  • The Case for Quantifying Sentience in Animal Welfare by Damin Curtis
  • Consciousness in AI: Insights from the Science of Consciousness by Patrick Butlin et.a.

 

3.8. Physics

3.8.1 Environmental design and atmospheric engineering

Atmospheric and environmental engineering research could decouple human welfare from the suffering-laden dynamics of wild ecosystems, with the goal to allow biospheres to be managed with welfare concerns over utility priorities. 

3.8.2 Understanding the long-term future of the universe, incl. prevalence and expiration of inhabited planets, and respective s-risk and welfare concerns. 

3.9. Starting A Compassionate Impact Oriented Academic Journal

The journal should focus on cross-causal welfare of all sentient beings and would 

  • help evaluate biotechnological and other research for its potential contribution to suffering prevention, 
  • disseminate findings and application opportunities across disciplines, 
  • and promote the research itself. 

Research assessment criteria should include whether the research approach meets relevant ethical and quality standards, and could include whether work specifically targets scalable, long-term suffering prevention with a likely net-positive impact.

The research directions above share a common bottleneck: political engagement to translate findings into policies; the communities, institutions, and networks capable of acting on their findings are still underdeveloped relative to the scale of the problem. Building that capacity is the subject of the next section.

Compassionate Genomics for the 21st Century 

-

Genomic Welfare with Ethical Care for Moral Predispositions 

Table of Contents
